The approval was based on two Phase 3 RCTs (SURMOUNT-OSA) enrolling 469 patients. Reference: FDA Press Release, December 20, 2024.

# OSA + Obesity Authorization Guide

**Subtitle:** Prior Authorization Support

**Description:** Prior authorization criteria, CPT and ICD-10 codes, and payer-specific appeal language for tirzepatide (Zepbound) and semaglutide in obstructive sleep apnea with obesity.

**Logo URL:** https://d2xsxph8kpxj0f.cloudfront.net/310519663337677270/YV697raiZLNdvDJAKcbMqZ/osa-obesity-compass-logo-N55A2VT3VcNAsLtxrMFMqY.webp

**Compass Href:** /osa-obesity-compass

**Appeal Letter Href:** /osa-obesity-appeal-letter

**Guideline Source:** FDA Dec 2024 · SURMOUNT-OSA NEJM 2024 · AASM 2025

---

## FDA Approval Context — December 20, 2024

**Zepbound (tirzepatide)** received FDA approval on December 20, 2024 as the **first and only prescription medication** for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. The approval was based on two Phase 3 SURMOUNT-OSA trials (N=469) demonstrating 47.7–56.2% AHI reduction vs placebo at 52 weeks (*N Engl J Med.* 2024;391:1193-205).

**Semaglutide (Wegovy)** is NOT FDA-approved for OSA. It may be considered off-label for weight management in OSA patients who cannot tolerate tirzepatide, but payer coverage for the OSA indication specifically requires the Zepbound/tirzepatide FDA approval.

**Indication specifics**: Zepbound for OSA is indicated for adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) and moderate-to-severe OSA, WITHOUT type 2 diabetes. Patients with T2DM should use Mounjaro (tirzepatide for T2DM) or Ozempic/Wegovy (semaglutide).

---

## Prior Authorization Requirements — Zepbound (OSA Indication)

- **[Required] Confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA** — PSG or HSAT documenting AHI ≥15 events/hr. PSG report must be attached. Most payers require PSG (not HSAT) for Zepbound PA.
- **[Required] Obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²)** — Current BMI documented in medical record. SURMOUNT-OSA mean BMI was 38.8 kg/m². Some payers may require BMI ≥35.
- **[Required] No type 2 diabetes mellitus** — Zepbound OSA indication is specifically for patients without T2DM. Document A1c or fasting glucose confirming no T2DM.
- **[Required] No contraindications** — No personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 (MEN2). No prior acute/chronic pancreatitis.
- **[Required] PAP therapy status documentation** — Document either: (a) current PAP therapy use ≥3 months (adjunct indication), or (b) documented PAP intolerance/failure with reason (standalone indication).
- **[Required] Prior dietary/lifestyle weight loss attempt** — ≥1 documented unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. SURMOUNT-OSA inclusion criterion. Required by most commercial payers.
- **[Often Required] Prescriber specialty** — Sleep medicine specialist, pulmonologist, or obesity medicine specialist. Some payers require specialist prescriber for Zepbound OSA indication.
- **[Required] Lifestyle modification program enrollment** — Documentation of enrollment in or referral to structured dietary counseling and physical activity program. Required per FDA labeling.
- **[Required] Baseline AHI and weight documentation** — Baseline AHI (from PSG/HSAT) and baseline weight/BMI must be documented for monitoring response and continued authorization.
- **[Often Required] Continued authorization criteria** — Most payers require repeat PSG/HSAT at 12 months showing AHI improvement, and ≥5% body weight reduction from baseline.

---

## Common Denial Reasons & Response Language

**Denial: "Not medically necessary"**
Cite SURMOUNT-OSA Phase 3 RCT (NEJM 2024;391:1193-205): tirzepatide reduced AHI by 47.7–56.2% vs placebo (p<0.001), with 61–70% reduction in OSA-specific hypoxia burden. FDA granted Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, and Fast Track designations, approving Zepbound December 20, 2024 as the first and only pharmacologic treatment for OSA.

**Denial: "Experimental/investigational"**
Zepbound received full FDA approval on December 20, 2024 for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. This is not an investigational use. The approval was based on two Phase 3 RCTs (SURMOUNT-OSA) enrolling 469 patients. Reference: FDA Press Release, December 20, 2024.

**Denial: "Step therapy required — PAP not tried first"**
SURMOUNT-OSA Trial 1 specifically enrolled patients unable or unwilling to use PAP therapy and demonstrated significant AHI reduction (-47.7% vs placebo, p<0.001). FDA approval does not require prior PAP failure. Document clinical reasons for PAP intolerance/non-use and cite FDA labeling which approves Zepbound as standalone therapy.

**Denial: "BMI does not meet threshold"**
Patient BMI is [X] kg/m², meeting the FDA-approved threshold of ≥30 kg/m² for the Zepbound OSA indication. SURMOUNT-OSA enrolled patients with BMI ≥30 (mean 38.8 kg/m²). Attach current weight documentation.

**Denial: "No prior weight loss attempts documented"**
Patient has documented [X] prior dietary/lifestyle weight loss attempts: [describe attempts with dates]. This meets the SURMOUNT-OSA inclusion criterion of ≥1 unsuccessful dietary attempt. Attach medical records documenting prior attempts.

**Denial: "Preferred agent not tried (semaglutide step therapy)"**
Semaglutide (Wegovy) is NOT FDA-approved for OSA. Only tirzepatide (Zepbound) has an FDA-approved indication for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Requiring step therapy with a non-approved agent for this indication is clinically inappropriate. Cite FDA approval December 20, 2024.

---

## Tirzepatide (Zepbound) Dosing — OSA Indication

| Week | Dose | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| Weeks 1–4 | 2.5 mg SC weekly | Starting dose — titration phase |
| Weeks 5–8 | 5 mg SC weekly | Titrate if tolerated |
| Weeks 9–12 | 7.5 mg SC weekly | Titrate if tolerated |
| Weeks 13–16 | 10 mg SC weekly | Titrate if tolerated |
| Weeks 17–20 | 12.5 mg SC weekly | Titrate if tolerated |
| Week 20+ | 15 mg SC weekly (max) | Maximum tolerated dose; baseline AHI obtained at week 20 in SURMOUNT-OSA |

Administer subcutaneously in abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. Rotate injection sites. Titrate every 4 weeks to maximum tolerated dose. Reduce dose if GI side effects are intolerable.

---
